_comment: Real-landscape validation manifest (cosmo plan Phase 6 / §5b).
Small, TRACKED file. Names the DEM to fetch and where the authoritative
per-sample regression targets come from. NO large data is ever committed.
The DEM is fetched keyless via the lsdtt-fetch-raster CLI (Copernicus
GLO-30 on AWS / Microsoft Planetary Computer -- NO API key), clipped to the
bounding box below into a temporary workdir by
tests/scripts/run_cosmo_validation.py, and deleted after the run.
Regression targets are HARVESTED from OCTOPUS (v2.3) via WFS -- see
octopus_source below and the sample-table header for full provenance.
description: Dethier et al. (2014) Front Range 10Be basins. Pilot subset = a compact Boulder Creek / Front Range cluster of 14 small catchments (0.07-10.11 km2) deliberately spanning 1962-3480 m elevation, to (a) shake out the harness on a single modest DEM and (b) expose the elevation-dependent residual (see caveat below) before GB-scale Himalayan datasets.

published_reference.citation: Dethier, D.P., Ouimet, W., Bierman, P.R., Rood, D.H., Balco, G. (2014), Geology 42(2), 167-170.
published_reference.calculator: OCTOPUS v2.3 recalculation with CAIRN (Mudd et al. 2016; github LSDTopoTools_CRNBasinwide), default Stone/Lal 'St' scaling (EBE_* fields).

_comment: Regression targets (concentration, uncertainty, standard, denudation rate)
are harvested from OCTOPUS, NOT scraped from the paper and NOT invented.
OCTOPUS recalculates every rate with CAIRN -- the same algorithm
lsdtt-cosmo-tool implements -- so these are a NEAR-CAIRN oracle, not
bit-exact (see residual_expectation).
octopus_source.cql_note: Filter with CQL_FILTER, not bbox: the OCTOPUS server throws a ProjectionException on the WFS 2.0.0 bbox parameter.
octopus_source.scaling_scheme: St (Stone/Lal) -- EBE_MMKYR / EBE_GCMYR. OCTOPUS also stores EBEL/EBELNS (LSDn). Run lsdtt-cosmo-tool in the matching St scheme for a like-for-like compare; confirm the scheme flag at run time.

_comment: Simon 2026-07-24: agreement will NOT be exact. lsdtt3 has diverged from
the OCTOPUS/CAIRN configuration in three known ways (see
calculator_differences), plus a high-elevation production-scaling fix THIS
suite found (the S_tot>=1 clamp defect, plan §9b findings log).
residual_expectation.band: measured-then-frozen on the FIRST accepted network run; do NOT assert a tight zero-residual band. Record elevation_ave_m + octopus_area_km2 per basin in the summary.
residual_expectation.attribute_residual_to: muon-scheme + topographic-shielding + atmosphere differences (calculator_differences) + high-elevation scaling + DEM product (COP30 vs the DEM in the OCTOPUS recalculation) + basin pixel binning -- NOT to bugs.

_comment: Simon 2026-07-24: the THREE concrete config differences between lsdtt3's
default run and OCTOPUS's CAIRN recalculation, and a quantified consistency
check (same COP30 DEM, muon scheme toggled, topo shielding applied per-basin;
12 delineation-reliable basins). E scales ~linearly with production and with
topo_shield_value (verified: E ratio 0.98864 at topo=0.9885).

muon_scheme.lsdtt3: BraucherBorchers (lsdtt3 default; updated Braucher2011 F + Borchers2016 P0)
muon_scheme.effect: lsdtt3 BraucherBorchers gives ~5.65% LOWER production/erate than Braucher on these basins (switching lsdtt3 to Braucher raised mean E by +5.65%). This is the DOMINANT named difference and matches Simon's 'lsdtt3 has lower production'.

topographic_shielding.octopus: per-pixel topographic shielding applied (BETOPO field; pilot mean 0.9885, range 0.942-0.999)
topographic_shielding.lsdtt3: IGNORED (topo_shield_value default 1.0; no per-pixel topo shielding computed)
topographic_shielding.effect: ignoring shielding makes lsdtt3 erate HIGHER by ~(1/BETOPO - 1): ~+0.7% mean on the reliable basins, but up to +6% in the steepest/most-shielded basin (S169WTS036, BETOPO 0.942). octopus_topo_shield is recorded per basin in the sample table.
topographic_shielding.caveat: Simon 2026-07-24: OCTOPUS shielding is computed PIXEL-BY-PIXEL, so the basin-average BETOPO used here UNDER-captures it -- our correction applies one basin-mean factor, whereas the true effect is the production-WEIGHTED average of per-pixel shielding (steep, high-production ridgelines are shielded more). So the +0.7% is a LOWER BOUND on the real topo-shielding contribution; lsdtt3 computes no per-pixel topo shielding at all, so it cannot yet reproduce OCTOPUS's exactly.

atmosphere.lsdtt3: ERA40 (Balco/Lifton, latitude-dependent lapse) by default; NCEP now available via `atmosphere: NCEP`
atmosphere.effect: QUANTIFIED 2026-07-24: running lsdtt3 with NCEP instead of ERA40 raises erate by +0.64% mean (range +0.44 to +0.89%), and the shift is ELEVATION-DEPENDENT (+0.44% at 2115 m -> +0.89% at 3480 m). Small, smooth, mostly systematic -- mean|delta| vs OCTOPUS barely moves (4.98 -> 4.92). NCEP support added to lsdtt3 (crn_parameters.nc ncep_* grids + atmospheric_pressure_ncep, a port of Balco NCEPatm_2); ERA40 remains the default and the sentinel is bit-unchanged.

consistency_check_2026_07_24.conclusion: All THREE named differences are now quantified. Muon dominates (+5.65%); topo shielding (-0.70% mean, up to -6% steep) and atmosphere (+0.64%, elevation-dependent) are small. Muon and topo act in OPPOSITE directions and partly cancel, so lsdtt3's near-zero baseline (-0.97%) is partly coincidental cancellation. Matching ALL THREE does NOT drive agreement to zero -- it OVERSHOOTS to ~+4.5% (D), so a residual ~+4-4.5% net SURPLUS in lsdtt3 remains that these three do NOT explain: it must come from production P0 values (Braucher2011/Borchers2016 vs OCTOPUS's exact P0), the COP30-vs-original DEM (basin hypsometry), the high-elevation scaling fix, and delineation. The per-basin SCATTER (mean|delta| ~5%) is nearly INSENSITIVE to all three uniform corrections (4.98 -> 4.95 -> 4.80 -> ~4.9), confirming the scatter is SPATIAL (DEM resolution/delineation), not the muon/topo/atmosphere systematics.

dem.dem_source_note: Keyless. Driven through the lsdtt-fetch-raster CLI, which retrieves and clips Copernicus GLO-30 from AWS Open Data (dem_source: cop30_aws) or Microsoft Planetary Computer (dem_source: planetary_computer) with NO account or API key. Set dem_source to planetary_computer to use the PC STAC mirror instead.
dem.target_epsg_note: UTM 13N (EPSG:32613) for the Colorado Front Range; matches OCTOPUS PROJEPSGID for these S169 basins. The cosmo CLIs require a PROJECTED CRS, so the DEM is warped to UTM at fetch time.
dem.resolution_choice_note: COP30 (30 m) vs the DEM used in the OCTOPUS/CAIRN recalculation is a DOCUMENTED, attributable difference in the validation (DEM resolution + product), not a bug -- record it alongside the production-scheme residual in the summary.

bounding_box._comment: Union of the 14 pilot basins' OCTOPUS outline footprints, padded ~0.02 deg. Covers the whole cluster in one modest DEM.

_comment: lsdtt-cosmo-tool run knobs for this dataset. The default
threshold_contributing_pixels (1000 = 0.9 km2 at 30 m) is TOO HIGH for
these sub-km2 Front Range catchments: it snaps small outlets onto a much
larger channel, inflating the basin and wrecking the comparison, and skips
basins that never reach 1000 px. Lowered here so small basins delineate
near their true size. Basins below ~this*cellsize remain unreliable (outlet
snap cannot resolve a catchment smaller than the threshold) and are flagged
in the summary; that is a delineation limit, not a numeric bug.
